Wang 9 in the corner-based system means the NW and NE corners are the "from" biome (shallow_water) — so it shows partial beach/sand on the SW/SE corners. The player is standing on the sand part of the tile but the biome says shallow_water.

This is a fundamental duality: the Wang tile visually shows a mix of biomes (part water, part beach), but the game logic treats the entire tile as a single biome (shallow_water). The player standing on the sand-looking portion of the tile would still be treated as being in shallow_water.

The user asks: "how do we handle interactions (will it eventually show the player as swimming even though it's a sand graphic?)"

This isn't something I can "fix" in the Wang tile system — it's a design question. The Wang tiles are visual only; the underlying biome data is what drives gameplay. On the transition edge between water and beach, tiles on the water side will show partial beach graphics, and tiles on the beach side will show partial water graphics. The player experiences the biome they're actually standing on, regardless of what the tile looks like.

My perspective to share with the user:
1. This is normal for any tile-based Wang system — transition tiles always show a mix
